gap: No result ChatGPT got gives a number measured by a named lab for any one-cable extender. The only full lab test I found is Notebookcheck's on an older FOPO 12-inch triple extender from 2022: 185 cd/m² at the center, 247:1 contrast and 79% sRGB, measured with an X-Rite i1Pro 2, and each of its screens needed its own power and video cable.
standout_why: I compared against TechRadar's KYY X90E review (cited), The Office Journal's USB-C extender list (no measurements, says only 'higher power draw over USB-C') and Dealectric's best-laptop-screen-extender page (in ChatGPT's results). Our page already credits Macworld for the Trio 3 Pro not reaching full brightness on laptop power and for the Duex Float 2 Pro's 80% cap at 7.5 W. TechRadar's KYY page shows the Performance headings 'Better than 300 nits' and '82% sRGB', but the text with the measurements did not load. Nothing in the results has a measured power draw in watts. The one complete lab measurement I found is of an older FOPO model that is not a current candidate, so it adds little and decides nothing.
decides: It confirms, rather than changes, the pick logic. Reviewers who named a result (Macworld, Android.com.pl) say a one-cable extender running on laptop power alone is brightness-limited, and the Trio 3 Pro needs Mobile Pixels' software plus a power adapter to run both screens from one cable at full brightness. That favors single-added-screen DisplayPort Alt Mode picks like the Duex Max DS for strict one-cable use. No named reviewer has measured the current FOPO S1, S7, S10 or S11, so measurements can't rank FOPO against Mobile Pixels or KYY. Notebookcheck's 2022 test of an older FOPO model can't be carried over to them.

findings.label: Brightness on laptop power alone (Macworld, Simon Jary, review dated 2026-04-02)
findings.value: Below maximum brightness without a power adapter
findings.note: Macworld: the screens 'can't draw enough power from the connected laptop to allow for maximum screen brightness'; for full brightness 'you need to attach a power adapter to one of the Trio's USB-C ports'. The reviewer found the capped brightness 'fine'. This is a reviewer observation, not a nits reading.

findings.label: One cable for both screens (Macworld, Simon Jary, 2026-04-02)
findings.value: Needs Mobile Pixels' software. Without it, base M1/M2 Macs (and the MacBook Neo) drive only one screen.
findings.note: Macworld: 'you need to install the software so that your can run both screens from the single cable connection'. It quotes the manual: no driver is needed 'if your laptop has two DP enabled USB-C ports'. With an adapter attached, 65 W passes through to the laptop.

findings.label: Brightness without external power (Android.com.pl, Łukasz Pająk, 2026-08-25)
findings.value: Maximum brightness limited in the on-screen menu unless the monitor has its own power
findings.source_title: Test Mobile Pixels Trio 3 Pro i Float 2 (Android.com.pl)
findings.note: Hands-on test of the Trio 3 Pro and Duex Float 2 Pro. It gives no colorimeter or wattage figures, only the maker's specs (Trio 3 Pro 300 nits per panel, Float 2 Pro 350 nits).

findings.label: One-cable operation and Mac support (TechRadar, Mark Pickavance, 2026-01-31)
findings.value: One USB-C cable (DisplayPort Alt Mode) carries video to both 15.6-inch screens plus power; does not work with MacBooks
findings.source_title: I tested the KYY X90E laptop screen extender (TechRadar)
findings.note: TechRadar: 'That one cable supports ALT-DP to send data to both screens, and also power'. It lists 'No Apple MacBook support' as a con. A 5 V 3 A (15 W) adapter is included to power the screens directly. The Performance section's headings read 'Better than 300 nits' and '82% sRGB', but the measurement text did not load in three reads, so neither figure is used here as a measured value.

findings.product: FOPO 12-inch Triple Monitor Extender (2022 model, not a current candidate)
findings.label: Measured brightness, contrast and gamut (Notebookcheck, Allen Ngo, 2022-07-23)
findings.value: 185 cd/m² center, 177.4 cd/m² average, 85% uniformity; 247:1 contrast; 79% sRGB; ColorChecker ΔE 4.59
findings.source_title: FOPO 12-inch triple monitor extender review: Clunky and more fragile than standalone portable monitors (Notebookcheck)
findings.note: Measured with an X-Rite i1Pro 2 (gamut via Argyll, ΔE via Calman) on a 2022 HP Pavilion Plus 14. No power draw reported. Notebookcheck: 'each of the two displays require their own cables for power and video'; the best case is one USB-C cable per screen on a laptop with two USB-C ports that carry DisplayPort video. This is an older FOPO model, and the figures must not be applied to the S1, S7, S10 or S11.

unsourced: Measured brightness, gamut or power draw for the Duex Max DS: Amateur Photographer (search result says a Datacolor Spyder X2 found 64% sRGB on the original Duex Max), Root-Nation (Duex Max DS) and TechPowerUp (Duex Max) all returned HTTP 403, so no figure is used.

Any meter-measured power draw in watts over one USB-C cable for any candidate (Duex Max DS, Trio 3 Pro, KYY X90E, FOPO S1/S7/S10/S11): an extended search found only unattributed ranges on SEO and seller pages. The 4.5 W Duex Max figure is Mobile Pixels' spec, not a measurement.
